hero.titleAria: Out of the group chat. Into one place.
hero.subtitle: Your group's projects, tasks, documents and plans, in one place. Instead of across a group chat, two spreadsheets, an email thread from March, and the head of whoever's been doing this the longest.
hero.freeBody: Your account is free, and every community you start gets a 30 day free trial.

tools.title: Learn one tool, know the rest
tools.description: Everything in a community is a tool. They're shared, tagged and commented on the same way, so the second one feels familiar before you've opened it.
tools.note: Switch on the ones your group needs. Switching one off later deletes nothing.
tools.projects: Boards, tables and calendars of the same tasks, with confetti if you want it.
tools.documents: Pages, spreadsheets and whiteboards you edit together live.
tools.queues: Keep track of whose turn it is, since apparently it's always nobody's.
tools.counterGroups: Tickets sold, cakes promised, chairs still missing.
tools.calendars: Events with RSVPs and reminders, so you're not the one reminding everyone.
tools.dashboards: Your numbers on one screen, and people only see what they have access to.
tools.wikis: Write down what the group knows, with links that keep working after a rename.
tools.posts: Announcements that don't get buried, with polls and read receipts.
tools.galleries: The photos from the day, together instead of in six people's camera rolls.

hangout.description: Post the news, run a poll, plan Saturday's game and see who's coming, all in the same place you keep the stuff that needs doing. It works the same for a rec league, a volunteer crew or the group that's been meeting for coffee since 2009.
hangout.drawingAria: A drawing of a community on Initiative

community.name: Eastside Rec Soccer
community.tagline: Sunday league, all ages, all skill levels

post.body: Season kickoff cookout this Saturday right after the game. Bring a chair and whoever you live with.

hangout.reply: I can bring the big grill if someone helps me lift it

points.planBody: Make an event, see who's going, and let the reminders do the nagging. A weekly game and a once-a-year fundraiser work the same way.
points.loopBody: Posts that stay pinned, polls people actually answer, and a list of who still hasn't read the announcement.
points.aroundBody: Online, idle or busy at a glance, with private messages that are end-to-end encrypted.

directory.title: Looking for a new crowd?
directory.description: Some communities list themselves publicly. Once you've got an account you can browse them by category, see how many people are around, and join one straight from the card.
directory.signUp: Sign up to browse them all
directory.signIn: Sign in to browse them all
directory.age: You need to be 16 or over to join a listed community.

dice.name: Dice & Dragons
dice.description: Weekly one-shots for people who can't commit to a whole campaign.

producers.name: Bedroom Producers
producers.description: Share what you're working on and borrow each other's drum sounds.

volleyball.name: Saturday Beach Volleyball
volleyball.description: Pickup games every Saturday morning, all levels welcome.

between.title: And the bits in between
between.description: These work the same way in every tool.

comments.title: The conversation sits on the thing
comments.body: Comments, replies and reactions live on the task or doc they're about, so the next person can actually find them.
comments.author: Sam
comments.text: can you check the float still has a wheel

mine.title: Everything with your name on it
mine.body: One account for the band, the PTA and the day job, and one list of everything you've said you'd do.

search.title: Find the thing you half remember
search.body: Ctrl K searches docs, spreadsheets, whiteboards and comments, and it's fine if you spell it wrong.

relations.title: Things know what they're connected to
relations.body: Link anything with #, mark what's blocking what, and backlinks show up on their own.

notify.title: Notifications that know when to shut up
notify.body: Bell, email or push, set per group, with quiet hours because nobody needs the PTA at 2am.

messages.title: Messages nobody else can read
messages.body: One-to-one or group chats, end-to-end encrypted so the server can't read them either.
messages.m1: did you tell them about the thing

safe.title: You cannot break this
safe.body: Deleted something? It goes to the Trash and you can get it back. Moved a task somewhere daft? Move it back, nobody saw.

closer.title: Your group's not on here yet?
closer.body: Starting a community takes about a minute. Make one board, add a few tasks, and send people the link.
closer.selfHost: Run it on your own server

download.title: Download
download.description: It runs in a browser, and using it that way forever is a completely respectable life choice. But it can also have its own icon and its own window.
download.androidBody: Installs like anything else, no app store needed.
download.iosBody: Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. It's the same Initiative, but iPhones don't get push notifications yet.
download.desktopBody: Its own window and its own icon in the dock or taskbar. It installs straight from the browser.
download.version: Version {{version}}, the one this server runs

android.title: Android
android.body: Let <1>Obtainium</1> keep it updated for you.
android.bodyPush: Push notifications included. Or let <1>Obtainium</1> keep it updated for you.

desktop.title: Computer
desktop.body: Chrome and Edge install it in one click. In Safari it's File, then Add to Dock.

browser.title: Browser
browser.body: Nothing to install, just bookmark it.

download.updatesBody: Initiative keeps itself up to date, so you won't need to come back here.
download.accountBody: Sign in on your phone, laptop or the library computer and everything's there.
download.passkeysBody: Sign in with a passkey if you'd rather not type a password.
